summary: A consent manager for your own site: an inventory of every script you load, gating so nothing non-essential runs before consent, an accessible banner with equal-weight accept and reject, withdrawal, Consent Mode signals and an optional consent log. First question: do you load anything non-essential at all? If not, the right build is no banner.

stack.why: no third-party script to consent to
to show what was agreed, without IPs

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: A list of every third-party script on your site
prerequisites.why: Phase 1 gates them by category. You cannot gate what you have not listed.
prerequisites.get: Open DevTools > Network on a cold load and write down every third-party host and what it does.

prerequisites.name: Do you need a banner at all?
prerequisites.why: Cookieless analytics and no ad or social scripts means no banner is the correct build.

prerequisites.name: Google Tag Manager or gtag (optional)
prerequisites.why: Phase 4 sends Consent Mode v2 signals if you use Google tags.

env.name: CONSENT_LOG_ENDPOINT
env.where: Optional endpoint for consent records. Empty disables logging.

phases.title: Inventory
phases.goal: scripts.json and every non-essential tag inert before consent.

steps.do: Write scripts.json with category and cookies per script
Change non-necessary script tags to type=text/plain with data-category

check: With the banner unanswered, the network tab shows zero requests to analytics or marketing hosts on a cold load

phases.title: The banner
phases.goal: Accept all, Reject all, Preferences with equal weight; stored with a version and timestamp.

steps.do: Build the accessible banner with no pre-ticked boxes
Store the choice in a first-party cookie and localStorage; activate gated scripts on accept without a reload

check: Reject leaves every gated script inert
Accept activates them without a reload

phases.title: Preferences and withdrawal
phases.goal: Reopen, re-ask on change, stop and clear on withdrawal.

steps.do: A footer link reopening preferences; a consent version bump when scripts.json changes
On withdrawal, stop scripts on next load and clear their cookies

check: Withdrawing stops the scripts and clears their cookies

phases.title: Consent Mode and the log
phases.goal: Google signals and an optional record without IPs.

steps.do: Send Consent Mode v2 defaults and updates when Google tags exist
POST consent id, timestamp, version and choices to CONSENT_LOG_ENDPOINT when set

check: The tag manager receives the consent state
The log shows one row per decision with no IP

phases.title: Verify
phases.goal: A checklist someone else can run.

steps.do: A test page and checklist: cold load, reject, accept, withdraw
README stating scripts.json is the source of truth and that this is engineering, not legal advice

check: Someone else runs the checklist and every step passes

phases.title: Keep it honest
phases.goal: Catch the tag someone adds next Tuesday.

steps.do: A CI check that fails when a third-party host appears in the built site that is not in scripts.json

check: Adding an unlisted script fails CI

product.outcome: Consent you can explain line by line, with the scanner replaced by a CI check on your own build.

architecture.swap: Any UI over the same stored choice

operations.backup: The repo; the log if kept.
operations.incident: An unlisted tracker found: remove it, bump the consent version.

notIncluded: Scanning for cookies you do not know about, jurisdiction-specific legal text, a regulator-familiar audit trail.
after: A per-region default (no banner where none is required)
